name: Chicken Tikka
subtitle: yogurt and spice marinated chicken, charred at the edges and still juicy inside

ingredients.note: thigh, not breast: it survives the heat
watery yogurt slides off the meat

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled
ingredients.note: the smoke point kills its raw pungency

prepNotes: Marinate twice. A short salt and lemon rub first, then the yogurt marinade, gives seasoning through the meat rather than only on the surface.
Hang the yogurt in a cloth for 30 minutes. This is the single change that stops the marinade sliding off in the oven.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with lemon juice, salt and half the chilli powder. Rest 20 minutes.
Whisk the hung yogurt with the ginger, garlic, remaining spices, kasuri methi and the cooled mustard oil until smooth.
Fold the chicken through and refrigerate at least 4 hours, better overnight.
steps.tip: Longer than 12 hours and the yogurt starts to break the meat down.

steps.text: Thread onto skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces so the heat gets round them.
steps.tip: Crowded skewers steam instead of charring.

steps.text: Cook at the highest heat your oven allows, around 240C, for 12 minutes. Turn once, baste with the leftover marinade and give it 5 minutes more.
Finish under a grill or over a direct flame for 2 minutes to get the char, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon.
steps.tip: The char is the point. Without it this is just baked chicken.

storage: Best within the hour. Cooked tikka keeps 2 days refrigerated and reheats acceptably in a hot pan, not a microwave. The raw marinated chicken freezes well for a month.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
